title: Linux.Mirai_Incident_Response_773
description: Investigate and respond to a potential compromise involving the Linux.Mirai trojan on a victim host.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has exhibited unusual behavior, including unexpected outbound network connections and suspicious scheduled tasks. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential compromise involving the Linux.Mirai trojan.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- IP Address: 192.168.60.10
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- IP Address: 192.168.60.10
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the victim host for unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system. Enumerate running services and identify any that appear unauthorized or suspicious.
levels.solution: Check the status of all services and look for any that are not part of the standard system configuration. Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and `systemctl status <service_name>` to check the status of specific services.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the status of all services and look for any that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and `systemctl status <service_name>` to check the status of specific services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system configuration and appear suspicious.

levels.title: Identify Scheduled Tasks
levels.content: Determine if any scheduled tasks or timers are responsible for automatically executing unauthorized processes. Identify scheduled execution persistence mechanisms that might be used to maintain unauthorized access.
levels.solution: Examine the systemd timers and services to find any that are not part of the standard system configuration. Use commands like `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers and `systemctl status <timer_name>` to check the status of specific timers.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd timers and services to find any that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers and `systemctl status <timer_name>` to check the status of specific timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that are not part of the standard system configuration and appear suspicious.

levels.title: Locate Suspicious Files
levels.content: Locate files installed by the unauthorized processes on the compromised host. Correlate suspicious activity with files introduced by the unauthorized processes.
levels.solution: Search for files in unusual or hidden directories that might be related to the suspicious services or scheduled tasks. Use commands like `find / -name '*.sh' 2>/dev/null` to search for specific file types and `ls -la /path/to/directory` to list files in specific directories.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Search for files in unusual or hidden directories that might be related to the suspicious services or scheduled tasks.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `find / -name '*.sh' 2>/dev/null` to search for specific file types and `ls -la /path/to/directory` to list files in specific directories.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for files in directories like /usr/local/lib/.netd that might be related to the suspicious activity.
